subject: CR estimation between pairs of modules

messages.author: 17fcbd0028caa7a5
messages.subject: CR estimation between pairs of modules
parts:
Dear all
I have eight partitions (modules). I used modularity.test to estimate the CR coefficient, which is an overall value. Now I would need to estimate CR for each par of partitions (all possible combinations).
How can I do that?
Thanks in advance
Alicia

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] CR estimation between pairs of modules
parts:
Alicia,

 

All possible pairwise combinations are already calculated using ‘modularity.test’. If you call your object, say ‘out’, they are found in ‘out$CR.mat’. 

 

Dean

messages.author: 59b6ecdf09b4ebce
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] CR estimation between pairs of modules
parts:
Hi Alicia,

I got some help on something similar not long ago. I was advised to compare the points associated with each module on a test by test basis. I only had three partitions, of which I combined the GPAs and matched the taxon names.

comb.lm<-combine.subsets(one=one.gpa, two=two.gpa, three=three.gpa, gpa=TRUE)
dimnames(comb.lm$coords)[3] <- dimnames(one.gpa$coords)[3]

Then, if yours was anything like mine, I had a landmark group with all partitions:
land_all.gps<-c("1","1"...."2","2"..."3","3",...)

And for each of my individual comparisons:

land_1vs2.gps<-c("1","1",..."2",2",...)
land_1vs3.gps<-c("1","1",..."3",3",...)
etc...

Then the command for doing the CR for each:
mod_1vs2<-modularity.test(comb.lm$coords, partition.gp=land_1vs2.gps, CI = FALSE, iter=499)

And so on for each pair. Hopefully that works for you like it did for me.

Best,
Bob
